description: Reports the state of a specification package: its lifecycle status, whether it validates, every task with its state and whether it is ready, the next task to work on, the lifecycle moves allowed from its status, and the packages it depends on and that depend on it. With --validate, the format's full verdict on the package; with --list, every package under the spec root; with --next, the package to implement now, the first open package in dependency order whose dependencies are finished, or that every package is done. With --task and --state it moves one or more tasks through the task state machine, every one or none, and writes the package's progress.json and no other file. With --status it moves the package through its lifecycle: activates, seals, archives or supersedes it (with --by, the package that replaces it), and moves an archived or superseded package under archive/. With --render it writes the package's spec.md, its render, and no other file. With --migrate it converts a version 2 package to version 3 in place. With --gate task or full it runs the package's linter, then its all_tests command, with no shell, and answers with one verdict, pass, fail or not_run, reusing a pass recorded for the same tree; with --gate-report it sums the package's gate runs since a commit. Without these it changes nothing. spec writes a package from an idea, specr renders one, speca reports and changes its state.

input.description: Exactly one reference to a spec package: a path to its directory or to a file inside it, or a directory name, spec number or spec name under the spec root (16_indexed_code_search, 16, indexed_code_search). None with --list or --next, and none with --render or --migrate for every package; --gate and --gate-report need one.

all.description: with --list, also list the packages under archive/, marked archived; with --render or --migrate and no input, also render or migrate them

base.description: with --gate task, the commit the task's change started from, which replaces {base} in the package's affected_tests command (default HEAD)

by.description: with --status superseded, the package that replaces this one, named as the input is; it must be a draft, active or sealed package, and when it can be saved its supersedes list gets this package's id

clean-env.description: with --gate, run every command with an empty temporary HOME, no global or system git configuration and GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, every other variable inherited; the directory is removed when the gate ends

dir.description: the repository the spec root and a relative reference are resolved against

dry-run.description: with the task form, the status form (--status), the render form (--render) or the migrate form (--migrate), run every check and report what would change, and write nothing

evidence.description: the evidence form, with --task and one task id: run every test of this evidence file once and record, for a task in progress of a package that requires evidence, the run in which each test failed before the task is implemented; the file is {"evidence": [{"covers": <criterion id, or path id for the integration task>, "tests": [<identifier>...], "no_red": <reason, for an exemption>}]}, at most 1 MiB

force.description: with the task form and the state done or pending, set a state the task state machine refuses, through the library's own bypasses, and skip the guard on keys the schema does not know; with the status form (--status), skip the checks that an activation validates, that no task is open when sealing, and that no key the schema does not know would be dropped; it skips nothing else, and a high task_state_forced, spec_invalid or tasks_open warning says what it skipped

gate.description: the gate form: run the package's linter command, then its all_tests command, from its test_commands, in --dir, each started directly with no shell, and answer with one verdict, pass, fail or not_run; task or full, the gate's level, which is part of the answer; whatever the package's status, and writing nothing under --dir

gate-report.description: the gate report: sum the package's gate runs recorded since a commit (--since, or the merge base of HEAD and the base branch): the full and task runs, their seconds and how many were reused, the full gate's seconds at the baseline and on the last tree, and the last full gate's slowest units; whatever the package's status, and writing nothing

list.description: list every package under the spec root, in number order, each with its status, whether it validates, its task counts and its next task; takes no input

migrate.description: the migrate form: convert a version 2 package to version 3 in place, whatever its status, by the rules of format v3 §13; a version 3 package is left alone; each package is reported written, unchanged or failed

next.description: name the package to implement now: the first package under the spec root, in dependency order with ties broken by number, that is open (draft or active, with a task pending or in progress) and whose every dependency is finished; all_done says when nothing is left, waiting what cannot start and why; a dependency cycle fails the call; takes no input

render.description: the render form: write the package's spec.md, the render every save writes beside its artifacts, whatever its status, and no other file; each package is reported written, unchanged or failed

since.description: with --gate-report, the commit the runs are counted from: a run at it or at a descendant of it that HEAD reaches, or MERGE_HEAD while a merge is uncommitted, counts; default the merge base of HEAD and the branch refs/remotes/origin/HEAD names, else main

specs-dir.description: where NN_name packages live; default <dir>/.specs or $AF_SPEC_DIR

state.description: the task form: the state to move the tasks to: pending, in_progress, done or dropped

status.description: the status form: move the package to this lifecycle status: active (computes the intent hash), sealed, archived or superseded (which needs --by); archived and superseded packages are moved under archive/. A move the lifecycle does not allow is refused, with the moves that are allowed

strict-handoffs.description: with --validate, report each handoff another package addresses to this one that no task takes as an error (handoff_not_taken) instead of a warning; it stores nothing

task.description: the task form: move these tasks to --state, every one or none; a task id, several ids comma-separated or repeated, next (the task to work on now) or all (every task not already in that state and not dropped)

timeout.description: with --gate, how long one command may run, a Go duration greater than zero; a command still running then is ended with every process it started, and the gate fails

validate.description: give the format's full verdict on the package: the schemas, the cross-file rules C1 to C8 and the cross-spec rules that concern it, each finding naming its rule; a package that does not validate is still a successful call

tool.description: the command that wrote this envelope

ok.description: true only when the command did the whole job it was asked to do; never true beside a non-zero exit_code or an error

status.description: the outcome in words, derived from exit_code: done (0), failed (1) or usage (2)

exit_code.description: the process exit code: 0 done, 1 failed, 2 usage error

summary.description: one sentence on the outcome, at most 200 characters

error.description: what failed and where; present exactly when ok is false

category.description: the kind of failure, which says whether re-running could help; an open set

retryable.description: whether re-running the identical command could succeed

resumable.description: whether re-running the same input continues the work rather than starting it over

fix_hint.description: a mechanical remedy, where one is known

env.description: the environment variables, one of which supplies what is missing

valid.description: the values the flag accepts here

current.description: the flag's value on this run

warnings.description: what went differently than intended without stopping the run

code.description: a stable code naming the cause; an open set

severity.description: high when the result is not quite what it appears to be, low when informational

spec_dir.description: the package directory, relative to --dir when inside it, absolute otherwise; runnable as the input of specr and speca; the report and the verdict

spec_id.description: the spec id, from the PRD frontmatter; the report and the verdict

spec_name.description: the spec name, from the PRD frontmatter; the report and the verdict

title.description: the spec title, from the PRD frontmatter; the report and the verdict

status.description: the package's lifecycle status: draft, active, sealed, superseded or archived; the report and the verdict

created_at.description: when the package was created, RFC 3339, from the PRD frontmatter; the report and the verdict

updated_at.description: when a task of the package last changed state, RFC 3339, from progress.json; absent when none has; the report and the verdict

profile.description: the package's profile, full or lite, from the PRD frontmatter; absent when the frontmatter names none, which is full

intent_hash.description: the SHA-256 of the PRD's ## Intent section, recorded when the package was activated; absent while unset

contract_hash.description: the SHA-256 of each contract file, keyed requirements.json and tasks.json, over its canonical encoding without extension keys, recorded when the package was activated; absent for a draft and for a package activated without it; the report and the verdict

contract_drift.description: for a package with a contract_hash, true when requirements.json or tasks.json no longer hashes to it, so that every task change, every evidence call and sealing are refused, and false when both match; absent for a package without a contract_hash; the report and the verdict

evidence_required.description: true when the package is active and has a contract_hash, so that each task closes on evidence: a test per criterion seen failing, then passing; absent otherwise; the report and the verdict

supersedes.description: the spec ids this package supersedes; absent when it supersedes none

valid.description: whether the package validates. In the report, its own verdict, from the schemas and the cross-file rules C1 to C8; with --validate, the combined verdict: true exactly when no error was kept from the package's own rules or the cross-spec rules. Absent under --list, where each entry holds its own

failing_rules.description: the rules the package's errors break, in order of first appearance; the report only, and present only when valid is false

intent_drift.description: true when the package is active, has an intent_hash, and its PRD's ## Intent section no longer hashes to it or is gone, so that every save is refused; absent otherwise; the report and the verdict

tasks.description: every task of the plan, in order, the derived integration task last, with its state and whether it is ready; [] when the plan has none; the report only

id.description: the task id, as --task takes it

kind.description: implement for a task of tasks.json, or integration for the derived last task of a full package

state.description: pending, in_progress, done or dropped, from progress.json

depends_on.description: the tasks that must be done first

ready.description: true for a pending task whose dependencies are all done; absent otherwise

evidence.description: speca's report only, never specr: in a package that requires evidence, the tests that cover each criterion the task owns, from progress.json; absent for a task that has none

covers.description: the id of a criterion the task owns, or for the integration task of an execution path

no_red.description: the exemption: why the entry's tests need not be seen failing first; absent when there is none

tests.description: the tests that cover it, each with the runs recorded of it

test.description: the test identifier, as the evidence command takes it

failed.description: the run in which speca saw the test fail; absent until then, and for an exempt test or one of the integration task

tree.description: the git tree id of the working tree the run was on, as the gate computes it; absent outside a git work tree

passed.description: the run in which speca saw the test pass when the task closed; absent until then

verdict.description: pass (every command exited 0, or a recorded pass was reused), fail (a command exited with another code or ran past --timeout) or not_run (a command could not start: its program was not found, its string could not be split, or test_commands names no such command); exit code 0 carries every verdict

artifacts.description: what the run produced, read off facts the command holds

kind.description: what the entry is; its other fields are the ones of its kind

dry_run.description: true when it would have been written but for --dry-run

next.description: the invocations a caller would plausibly make next

flags.description: the flags to add, each value its own element

why.description: why a caller would run it

duration_ms.description: wall-clock time of the run, in milliseconds

started_at.description: when the run started, RFC 3339 in UTC

exit_codes.0: reported: the state of a package, its verdict (a package that does not validate is reported too), the list of packages, the package to implement next (or that every package is done, or that none can start), the tasks moved, the status changed, what --render did to spec.md, what --migrate did to the package, the gate's verdict whatever it is (pass, fail or not_run), or the gate report
exit_codes.1: failed: the package could not be loaded, or the spec root --list reads could not be read; or the task form was refused after the package was read (the task state machine does not allow a move, the package can no longer take a write, a save would delete keys the schema does not know) or its write failed; the stage is named in error, and a refusal's result holds the package as it is on disk; or the status form was refused after the packages were read, with no result (the lifecycle does not allow the move, an activation has no intent or does not validate, a task is open, keys would be dropped, the replacing package is superseded or archived, the archive destination is taken) or its write failed; if only the move under archive/ failed, the status is written, the result says so and the call is resumable; or the render form's package could not be loaded or its spec.md could not be written, or the migrate form's package could not be read, converted or written, or the spec root a sweep reads could not be read, or the dependencies of the packages --next reads form a cycle, or the package the gate or the gate report reads could not be loaded, or the run log could not be read, or the commits since --since could not be listed (stage git)
exit_codes.2: usage error: the call is refused before anything is written: the reference names no package or two, two operations in one call, a flag that cannot hold, an id the plan does not have, --status draft, or a --by that names the package itself, no package or one with its spec_id, a --gate other than task or full, a --timeout that is not a duration greater than zero, a --base that names no commit or comes without --gate task, a package with affected_tests outside a git work tree at the task level, a --since that names no commit, no --since and no base branch, or a --gate-report outside a git work tree; nothing was written
